claim: Rice is one of the world's major staple crops and is an essential component of the diets and livelihood of over 3.5 billion people.
source: Rice (Oryza sativa), one of the world's major staple crops, is an essential component of the diets and livelihood of over 3.5 billion people (Wing et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wing et al., 2018, which provides external scholarly support for the statement.

claim: Genomics-based breeding combined with advanced technologies such as high-throughput field-based phenotyping is one of the most promising approaches to improve rice performance.
source: A large number of studies have investigated how the performance of rice can be improved, and genomics-based breeding, combined with other advanced technologies such as high-throughput field-based phenotyping, is one of the most promising approaches to improve the performance (Wing et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wing et al., 2018, indicating that this is an established view in the field.

claim: Previous studies have suggested that transcriptome dynamics of rice can be predominantly explained by endogenous factors and abiotic variables such as ambient air temperature and solar radiation.
source: Previous studies have investigated how meteorological and endogenous (e.g. plant age and genotype) variables influence the gene expression patterns (transcriptome dynamics) of rice under fluctuating field conditions (Kashima et al., 2021; Nagano et al., 2012), and have suggested that transcriptome dynamics can be predominantly explained by endogenous factors and abiotic variables such as ambient air temperature and solar radiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kashima et al., 2021 and Nagano et al., 2012, which provide external scholarly support.

claim: Biotic variables such as insect herbivory and microbial mutualists/pathogens play an important role in determining the transcriptome dynamics and productivity of crops.
source: Nonetheless, biotic variables such as insect herbivory and microbial mutualists/pathogens also play an important role in determining the transcriptome dynamics and productivity of crops (Cohen and Leach, 2019; Savary et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cohen and Leach, 2019 and Savary et al., 2019.

claim: The dynamics of biotic variables under field conditions are difficult to predict because they often show more complex, nonlinear dynamics than abiotic variables.
source: However, the dynamics of biotic variables (i.e. ecological community members) under field conditions are difficult to predict because they often show more complex, nonlinear dynamics than abiotic variables (Hsieh et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hsieh et al., 2005.

claim: eDNA metabarcoding is a cost- and time-effective means to detect a large number of species.
source: Previous studies have shown that eDNA metabarcoding, an approach to comprehensively amplify and sequence DNAs belonging to a target taxa in an environmental sample, is a cost- and time-effective means to detect a large number of species (e.g. Miya et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Miya et al., 2015.

claim: Quantitative eDNA metabarcoding enabled effective evaluation of intraspecific genetic diversity.
source: For example, quantitative eDNA metabarcoding enabled effective evaluation of intraspecific genetic diversity (Tsuji et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tsuji et al., 2020.

claim: Quantitative eDNA metabarcoding enabled frequent and comprehensive monitoring of community dynamics.
source: For example, quantitative eDNA metabarcoding enabled effective evaluation of intraspecific genetic diversity (Tsuji et al., 2020) and frequent and comprehensive monitoring of community dynamics (Ushio, 2022; Ushio et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ushio, 2022 and Ushio et al., 2023.

claim: Nonlinear time series analytical tools enable researchers to reconstruct complex interaction networks.
source: Second, nonlinear time series analytical tools enable researchers to reconstruct complex interaction networks (Chang et al., 2021; Deyle et al., 2016; Osada et al., 2023; Schreiber, 2000; Sugihara et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chang et al., 2021; Deyle et al., 2016; Osada et al., 2023; Schreiber, 2000; Sugihara et al., 2012.

claim: Five artificial rice plots were established in an experimental field at the Center for Ecological Research, Kyoto University, in Otsu, Japan in 2017.
source: Five artificial rice plots were established using small plastic containers (90×90 × 34.5 cm; 216 L total volume; Risu Kogyo, Kagamigahara, Japan) in an experimental field at the Center for Ecological Research, Kyoto University, in Otsu, Japan (34° 58′ 18″ N, 135° 57′ 33″ E) (Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text and describes the experimental setup.

claim: Rice seedlings (var. Hinohikari) were planted on 23 May 2017 and harvested on 22 September 2017 (122 days).
source: Sixteen Wagner pots (φ174.6–160.4 mm [top–bottom] × 197.5 mm; AsOne, Osaka, Japan) were filled with commercial soil, and three rice seedlings (var. Hinohikari) were planted in each pot on 23 May 2017 and then harvested on 22 September 2017 (122 days).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text and describes the experimental timeline.
